ruling_gist_en: A cooperative development of real estate contract refers to a contract entered into between parties for the cooperative development of a real estate project by making joint contributions in the form of land use rights, funds, or other means, sharing profits, and jointly bearing risks. The conversion of the land use rights contributed by the party providing them into common ownership of all cooperative parties or into the name of the project company is usually an important element of such a contract. full_text_en:
Changzhi Huamao Subsidiary Food and Fruit Co., Ltd. v. Changzhi Jiechang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Contract for Cooperative Development of Real Estate

【Ruling Summary】

A contract for cooperative development of real estate refers to a contract concluded between parties for the purpose of jointly investing in the form of provision of land use rights, funds, etc., sharing profits, and bearing risks in the cooperative development of a real estate project. The conversion of the land use rights contributed by the party providing the land to being jointly owned by all cooperative parties or attributed to the project company is usually an important aspect of such a contract. Whether a contract is a contract for cooperative development of real estate with the land use rights valued as capital contribution, or a simple contract for transfer of land use rights, should be determined based on whether the parties share profits and bear risks in the real estate development project.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2005) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 60

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Changzhi Huamao Subsidiary Food and Fruit Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 1, Beiguan Street, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Huachuan, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Tian Ruihua, Attorney at Law, Beijing Huamao Silicon Valley Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Han Ting, Attorney at Law, Beijing Hanheng Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Changzhi Jiechang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 302, Middle Changxing Road, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Su Fulun, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Gao Yuan, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhongrui Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Shuqin, Attorney at Law, Shanxi Shuangshi Law Firm.

In the case concerning the dispute over a contract for cooperative development of real estate between appellant Changzhi Huamao Subsidiary Food and Fruit Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huamao Company) and appellant Changzhi Jiechang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiechang Company), the Shanxi High People's Court rendered the Civil Judgment (2005) Jin Min Chu Zi No. 1 on June 5, 2005. Dissatisfied with the judgment, both Huamao Company and Jiechang Company appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing on September 20, 2005. Liu Huachuan, the legal representative of Huamao Company, and its agents ad litem Tian Ruihua and Han Ting, together with Su Fulun, the legal representative of Jiechang Company, and its agents ad litem Gao Yuan and Zhang Shuqin, appeared before the court to participate in the proceedings. This case has now been concluded.

Upon trial, the court of first instance found the following facts:

On August 22, 2001, the Changzhi City Construction Bureau of Shanxi Province submitted a request to the Changzhi Municipal People's Government of Shanxi Province based on the "Report on the Development and Renovation Plan for Huamao Commercial Park" submitted by the Changzhi City Urban District Subsidiary Food and Fruit Company. On November 28, 2001, the Changzhi Municipal Planning Commission approved the development of the Huamao District by the Changzhi City Urban District Subsidiary Food and Fruit Company with Chang Ji Tou Zi (2001) No. 216, setting the total construction area of the project at 43,787 square meters. On December 31, 2001, the Changzhi City Construction Commission of Shanxi Province issued a Site Selection Opinion Letter and a Construction Land Use Planning Permit to the Changzhi City Urban District Subsidiary Food and Fruit Company. On January 12, 2002, the General Office of the Changzhi Municipal People's Government of Shanxi Province issued a notice with Chang Zheng Ban Fa (2002) No. 1 for the demolition and renovation of the Huamao Commercial Park. On March 28, 2002, the Changzhi City Urban District Subsidiary Food and Fruit Company was changed and registered as Changzhi Huamao Subsidiary Food and Fruit Co., Ltd., with the legal representative before and after the change being Liu Huachuan. On April 21, 2002, Jiechang Company was registered and established, with Liu Huachuan as its legal representative. On April 27, 2002, the Changzhi Municipal Planning Commission of Shanxi Province approved the construction of the first-phase supermarket shopping center of the Huamao Commercial Park with a construction area of 28,380 square meters via Chang Ji Tou Zi (2002) No. 172.

On May 25, 2002, Huamao Company, Su Fulun, and Hong Kong Yiqun Enterprise Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hong Kong Yiqun Company) signed an "Agreement" stipulating the cooperative development of the Huamao Commercial Residential Park, but this agreement was not performed. On July 6, 2002, Huamao Company, Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen signed a "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" for the cooperative development of the Huamao Commercial Park project, stipulating that all parties agreed to cooperatively develop and construct the Huamao Commercial Park project, and the rights and obligations of each party would be regulated by this agreement. The main clauses include: First, the original Huamao Commercial Park project had been approved by documents including Chang Ji Tou Zi (2001) No. 216, Chang Jian Fa (2001) No. 136, Chang Zheng Ban Fa (2002) No. 1, and Chang Ji Tou Zi (2002) No. 172, and had obtained the Site Selection Opinion Letter No. Xuan Zhi 58 and the Construction Land Use Planning Permit No. Chang Tou 2001 Bianhao Yongdi 66. Now, due to the needs of project construction, after friendly negotiation among three parties, Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company were added to carry out the development and construction of the project. Second, the project land scope includes Huamao Company's own allocated land, namely, the land use area of 15,293.9 square meters under Chang Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 044 and the land use area of 2,451.2 square meters under Chang Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 014. Third, the development method was that the parties agreed to use Jiechang Company as the project company for the renovation and construction of the Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street; the equity of Jiechang Company's shareholders would be changed; Huamao Company should cooperate with Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company to handle the shareholder change registration procedures for Jiechang Company after the signing of this agreement, and the costs incurred would be paid by Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company. Fourth, the development conditions: according to the construction plan of the Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street, the project would be built in two phases and specifically implemented by Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company. Huamao Company was responsible for changing the original renovation and construction unit from Huamao Company to Jiechang Company for renovation, construction, and operation, and for handling all government approvals before the start of construction for Jiechang Company; the land areas of Huamao Company under Chang Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 044 (15,293.9 square meters) and Chang Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 014 (2,451.2 square meters) would be incorporated into the overall development and construction of the Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street by Jiechang Company; the land change procedures would be handled uniformly after the demolition agreement was signed; Huamao Company was responsible for the demolition, compensation, resettlement, and "three connections and one leveling" of the above-ground buildings on that part of the land according to the first and second phase development progress, and would bear the costs incurred (demolition deposit, moving, demolition, removal, and transport); Huamao Company would assist in handling the equity change procedures for Jiechang Company and in obtaining the real estate development and operation qualifications for Jiechang Company, with the necessary costs borne by Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company. Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company were responsible for the demolition, resettlement, and costs of the part of the land other than the project construction land provided by Huamao Company, and would pay the required land transfer fees for that part, be responsible for the investment of all funds required for the development, construction, and operation of this project except for the costs borne by Huamao Company, be responsible for the specific operation of Jiechang Company, and carry out the overall planning, design, construction, and sales of this project, and be responsible for the investment of its costs and the registered capital of the project company. Fifth, distribution and sales: Huamao Company would receive 11,070 square meters of property from the total construction area of the project, including 3,700 square meters of shopping mall in the first phase (as full compensation for the demolition and resettlement of the land under Chang Guo Yong (2001) No. 014 and its above-ground buildings), 500 square meters of independent storefronts, and 2,205 square meters of residential housing in the first phase; in the second phase, 1,000 square meters of shopping mall, 1,500 square meters of independent storefronts, and 2,165 square meters of residential housing; when the project started operating and the demolition announcement was issued, Jiechang Company and Huamao Company would sign a demolition and resettlement agreement according to the above conditions, with the specific location and level of the compensation property to be agreed upon in the overall project plan; except for the 11,070 square meters of property compensated to Huamao Company, all other property would belong to Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company; the properties obtained by each party would be relatively concentrated and well-matched, and each party would bear the various fees payable according to property management regulations. The agreement also stipulated property sales, liability for breach of contract, and time limits.

According to the above agreement, on July 7, 2002, the shareholders of Jiechang Company were changed from Liu Huachuan, Li Qinding, and Li Shuzhen to Liu Huachuan, Su Fulun, and Chen Peisen, and the legal representative was changed from Liu Huachuan to Su Fulun. On November 20, 2002, Jiechang Company obtained the land use rights for 19,983.19 square meters through allocation. On October 25, 2002, Jiechang Company applied to the Changzhi City Urban District Planning Commission of Shanxi Province: Jiechang Company had obtained the development rights for the Huamao project land sold by the municipal government through listing procedures such as registration, signed a state-owned land use rights transfer contract with the land department, paid the land transfer fee, and obtained the state-owned land use certificate; Jiechang Company had optimized and adjusted the project's planning and design, with a total construction area of 74,464 square meters, constructed in two phases; ... it applied for a change of project approval, establishing Jiechang Company as the project development entity, and applied to change the project name from "Huamao Commercial Park" to "Holiday Sunshine Plaza."

On November 1, 2002, Jiechang Company and Huamao Company signed a "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement." Main stipulations: In accordance with the "Implementation Measures for House Demolition Management of Changzhi City" and the provisions of Article V, Paragraph 1 of the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement," under the principle of fairness and good faith, the two parties signed the following agreement regarding matters related to demolition and resettlement: Jiechang Company would strictly follow Article V of the original "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" to provide resettlement compensation for Huamao Company's demolished houses. Given the lack of working capital of Huamao Company and the practical difficulties encountered in the current demolition work, the two parties, after negotiation and agreement, agreed that on the basis of the original agreement, Huamao Company would reduce its share of the first-phase residential building area by 800 square meters, and Jiechang Company would provide cash compensation at a price of 1,000 yuan per square meter of building area, i.e., Huamao Company would receive a total building area of 10,270 square meters (originally 11,070 square meters) and cash compensation of 800,000 yuan. The compensation properties should be relatively concentrated and well-matched, with the specific location, orientation, and level of the compensation property to be agreed upon in the design floor plan after the project design documents are finalized and approved. After this agreement was signed, Huamao Company could change the land use rights holder of the land area of 15,293.9 square meters under Chang Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 044 to Jiechang Company, and when the second-phase demolition began, change the land use rights holder of the land area of 2,451.2 square meters under Chang Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 014 to Jiechang Company. After the signing of this agreement, Huamao Company, as stipulated in the original "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement," was required to demolish the above-ground buildings within its land area and carry out site leveling and three connections (water, electricity, road) according to the project construction progress, and bear the corresponding costs and responsibilities. The agreement also stipulated matters regarding deposit, land use certificate, building permit, house ownership certificate, etc.

On December 31, 2002, based on Jiechang Company's application, the Changzhi Municipal Planning Commission of Shanxi Province issued a reply with Chang Ji Tou Zi (2002) No. 604: The project name was changed from the original "Huamao Commercial Park" to "Holiday Sunshine Plaza"; the construction unit was changed from Huamao Company to Jiechang Company; construction scale and main contents: the total land area of the project was 19,983 square meters, total construction area 74,464 square meters; total investment and funding sources: total investment for the project was 75 million yuan, all funds to be raised by Jiechang Company on its own. On June 19, 2003, Jiechang Company obtained the Construction Project Planning Permit. On August 11, 2003, the Changzhi Municipal Planning Commission of Shanxi Province issued a notice with Chang Ji Tou Zi (2003) No. 328, agreeing to change the project name "Holiday Sunshine Plaza" to "Triumph Capital Plaza."

On November 8, 2003, Huamao Company and Jiechang Company signed a "Supplementary Agreement." Based on the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" and the "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement," the two parties agreed on specific issues such as project distribution and compensation as follows: First, during the project operation, both parties should abide by the principles of mutual benefit, good faith, and legality, and matters concerning the interests of both parties should be transparent, communicated promptly, and negotiated. Second, the property area, location, and other matters compensated to Huamao Company should be compensated according to the provisions of the "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement." The specific types, orientations, areas, and levels of compensation were as follows: the compensation area and location numbers for large and small shopping malls and stores should be implemented according to the "Building Plan Location Allocation Plan" (Attachment 1) signed by both parties and the "Commercial Compensation Area and Location Number Table" (Attachment 2); the compensation area and location numbers for residential housing should be implemented according to the "Residential Compensation Area and Location Number Table" (Attachment 3) signed by both parties. The agreement also stipulated matters related to design changes: both parties agreed that the entire project should be constructed according to the complete set of construction drawings drawn by Shenzhen Design Decoration Engineering Co., Ltd. and approved by the Changzhi City Construction Management Department; Jiechang Company should submit one set of copies of the project approval documents, the "one document and two permits," and the construction permit to Huamao Company within 15 days after the signing of the agreement for safekeeping; all property compensated to Huamao Company by Jiechang Company should be treated as resettlement for returning households, and Jiechang Company should assist Huamao Company in handling property ownership certificates and land use rights certificates; the Huamao Commercial Park was to be developed as a whole by Jiechang Company, and the overall investment, planning, design, construction, and sales of the park were all to be the responsibility of Jiechang Company; however, according to the principle of cooperation, Jiechang Company should communicate with Huamao Company in a timely manner on the above issues, and for matters related to the design, construction, etc., of the property compensated to Huamao Company, Jiechang Company must seek the opinions of Huamao Company and obtain Huamao Company's approval, and must not act arbitrarily to harm Huamao Company's interests; this agreement had the same legal effect as the cooperation agreement of July 6, 2002, and previous agreements signed between the parties; in the event of any inconsistency or conflict between this agreement and previous agreements, this agreement shall prevail.

According to the agreements of the parties and the approval documents of government departments, Jiechang Company developed the project. After Huamao Company signed the supplementary agreement with Jiechang Company regarding the distribution of property, it claimed that it only then learned that the development area of Jiechang Company had increased from 43,787 square meters to 71,549.8 square meters. As a cooperative development entity, it requested distribution of the increased area, leading to a dispute between the parties.

On September 22, 2004, Huamao Company filed a lawsuit with the Changzhi Intermediate People's Court of Shanxi Province, and Jiechang Company raised a jurisdictional objection. On November 20, 2004, the Shanxi High People's Court ordered the case to be removed to the Shanxi High People's Court for trial with (2004) Jin Li Min Zhong Zi No. 77. Huamao Company claimed in its lawsuit: Huamao Company, as the development unit, developed the Huamao Commercial Park project, which was approved by the Changzhi Reform and Development Planning Commission of Shanxi Province with Chang Ji Tou Zi (2001) No. 216, with a total development and construction scale of 43,787 square meters. To develop the project, Huamao Company established Jiechang Company and handled the relevant development procedures. On July 6, 2002, according to relevant documents of the Changzhi Municipal People's Government of Shanxi Province, Huamao Company, as a land investment cooperative partner, signed the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" for the cooperative development of the Huamao Commercial Park project with Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen. After the agreement was signed, Huamao Company, relying on the trust of the cooperative partners and in accordance with the agreement, handled the change of registration and land procedures for Jiechang Company. Based on the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement," the two parties also signed a "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement" regarding the positioning and related issues of the property allocated to Huamao Company. In that agreement, it was also stipulated that Huamao Company would itself demolish the buildings on the 26.62 mu of land it provided.

Jiechang Company, as the cooperative representative of the cooperative partners Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen, and as the project company for the project, violated the principles of cooperation between the parties in its operation, keeping major matters concerning the project neither open nor transparent to Huamao Company. For example, major matters such as handling subsequent approval documents, design drawings and related materials, and changing the project name were all done arbitrarily by Jiechang Company, without seeking Huamao Company's opinions, providing information to Huamao Company, or even informing Huamao Company. Before September 2003, Huamao Company repeatedly raised objections and, regarding the distribution and positioning of property to Huamao Company, repeatedly requested Jiechang Company to provide complete drawings and related materials, but Jiechang Company refused to provide them. Later, after consulting, Huamao Company discovered that the design height of the shopping mall allocated to Huamao Company was unreasonably low, and that the project name had been unilaterally changed by Jiechang Company to "Triumph Capital Plaza," leading to a dispute between the parties. On November 8, 2003, the two parties signed the "Supplementary Agreement," which confirmed the operating principles of the parties and reached agreements on some of the disputed issues at that time and related issues. However, when negotiating and signing the agreement, Jiechang Company intentionally concealed the important fact that the construction scale of the project had been changed and increased to 71,549.8 square meters. Only on November 18, 2003, did Jiechang Company provide to Huamao Company the complete design drawings and relevant approval documents for the project, which was not in accordance with the provisions of Article V, Paragraph (2) of the "Supplementary Agreement." Thus, Huamao Company discovered that Jiechang Company had not only unilaterally changed the project name, but also, with the land area used by Huamao Company unchanged, unilaterally increased the total development and construction scale from the original 43,787 square meters to 71,549.8 square meters, an increase of 27,762.8 square meters, representing an increase ratio of 61.2%. The increased area was built on the 26.62 mu of land invested by Huamao Company and with bank loans secured by that invested land as collateral. Undoubtedly, Huamao Company's contribution was primary. According to the principles of cooperation and fairness, and considering the contribution, Jiechang Company should allocate an additional area of 13,881.4 square meters to Huamao Company, based on a 50% ratio of the new area, following the principle of good location and level matching and the proportions of various types of property areas. Huamao Company also argued that Jiechang Company's unilateral change of the project name constituted a breach of contract and harmed Huamao Company's legitimate rights and interests. Therefore, Huamao Company requested: 1. That Jiechang Company be ordered, on the basis of the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement" signed by both parties, to allocate to Huamao Company an additional total area of 13,881.4 square meters, comprising 5,480.38 square meters of residential housing, 2,508.37 square meters of independent stores, and 5,894.04 square meters of large and small shopping malls, based on a 50% ratio of the development and construction area increased unilaterally by Jiechang Company (27,762.8 square meters), and following the principle of good location and level matching for all types of property areas; 2. That Jiechang Company be ordered to jointly sign and seal with Huamao Company for all major decisions and all pre-sales and sales activities regarding the cooperative project, to avoid making it difficult to achieve the judgment; 3. That Jiechang Company be ordered to restore the project name "Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street" as agreed by both parties, to cease and cancel the project name "Triumph Capital Plaza" unilaterally changed by Jiechang Company and the pre-sales and sales activities conducted under that name, and to compensate Huamao Company for economic losses of 1 million yuan.

Jiechang Company argued in its defense: There is no contractual legal relationship of joint development between the parties; rather, the relationship is one of house demolition, relocation, and compensation under contract. First, Huamao Company has no right to claim 13,881.4 square meters of the developed building area beyond that specified in the Demolition and Relocation Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement. The Demolition and Relocation Agreement concluded between the parties marked the termination of the formal real estate joint development relationship and the establishment of a substantive relationship of house demolition, relocation, and compensation. Although the agreement was titled "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement," its content contained no provisions regarding the parties' capital contributions or respective proportions, and there existed no real estate cooperative relationship characterized by joint investment, joint operation, shared risks, and shared profits. The rights and obligations of the parties were established as those between the demolishing party and the demolished party under the Demolition and Relocation Agreement. During the development process, Jiechang Company provided relocation and compensation to all demolished parties (including Huamao Company), some of which have been fully performed and others are in the process of being performed. Although Huamao Company, having once acted as the project development entity, differed from other demolished parties, all of its interests have been fully relocated and compensated under the Demolition and Relocation Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement. Huamao Company is not currently a shareholder of Jiechang Company and therefore has no right to interfere with the company's decisions and operations, and even less right to dispose of developed building areas beyond those agreed upon in the agreements. According to the Real Estate Joint Development Agreement, the original reconstruction and construction entity was changed from Huamao Company to Jiechang Company, which proves that the development project has been transferred to Jiechang Company. The Supplemental Agreement constituted a further recognition of the demolition and relocation legal relationship between the parties under the Demolition and Relocation Agreement. The increase in area by Jiechang Company resulted from increased investment in multiple aspects and was a consequence of the company's business operations. If problems arose during the implementation of the revised planning and design, causing the company to incur operating losses, would Huamao Company also be required to bear 50% of the operating losses according to a baseless proportional share? Second, the premise of Huamao Company's claim regarding the "July 6" Agreement, that the total project area was 43,787 square meters, does not conform to the facts. Before the parties signed the agreement, they had already reached a consensus on the increase in project area. The signing of the "July 6" Agreement was based on the premise of modifying the original plan, and the relevant modification procedures were also handled with Huamao Company's cooperation. Therefore, Huamao Company's request for additional real estate distribution on the grounds of increased project area is entirely unfounded. Third, Huamao Company's lawsuit has exceeded the statutory exclusion period. Another reason Huamao Company filed the lawsuit against Jiechang Company seeking an increase in the distributed area was that the original agreement was "obviously unreasonable and unfair." As early as between October and December 2002, Liu Huachuan, the legal representative of Huamao Company, personally participated in the relevant procedures at the relevant authorities to handle the modification of related matters. From that point onward, Huamao Company had also waived this right through its own conduct. Fourth, Huamao Company has no right to require Jiechang Company to inform it or obtain its signature in matters such as the overall planning, design, and sales of this project. According to the Real Estate Joint Development Agreement, Jiechang Company is responsible for the overall planning, design, and sales of this project, as well as for the investment in related expenses and the registered capital of the project company. Moreover, the project company is a limited liability company, and major decision-making matters are only accountable to its shareholders, of which Huamao Company is not one. Fifth, Huamao Company's claim for compensation of RMB 1 million is entirely without basis; on the contrary, it should compensate Jiechang Company for substantial economic losses. Jiechang Company has neither engaged in any infringing acts nor any breach of contract, and there is no issue of compensating Huamao Company. In summary, Huamao Company, disregarding the substantial objective evidence demonstrating that the legal relationship between the parties is one of demolition, relocation, and compensation contract, claims an additional 13,881.4 square meters based on its assertion that it remains a cooperative party in the real estate joint development project. This exceeds the scope of compensation and relocation area established by the Demolition and Relocation Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement, and its request lacks both factual and legal basis. Furthermore, Huamao Company's lawsuit has exceeded the statutory exclusion period and should be dismissed according to law to protect the legitimate rights and interests of Jiechang Company.

The court of first instance, after trial, found that the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement" signed on July 6, 2002, by Huamao Company, Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen, as well as the "Demolition and Relocation Agreement" signed on November 1, 2002, by Huamao Company and Jiechang Company, and the "Supplemental Agreement" signed on November 8, 2003, all represented the true intentions of the respective parties, and no party raised any objection. Their legal validity should be confirmed, and all parties should strictly perform them. According to the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement," Huamao Company, as a party to the joint development, jointly signed the agreement and agreed to its obligations, namely, to demolish the above-ground buildings, achieve "three connections and one leveling" (water, electricity, road connections and site leveling), and bear the costs incurred therefrom. Therefore, Huamao Company should be recognized as a joint development entity for the project. The "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement" also stipulated that Jiechang Company would serve as the project company for the reconstruction and construction of the "Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street." The original reconstruction and construction entity was changed from Huamao Company to Jiechang Company for reconstruction, construction, and operation. Except for the costs of "three connections and one leveling" borne by Huamao Company, Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company were responsible for all capital investment required for the development, construction, and operation of this project, as well as for the specific operation of Jiechang Company and the overall planning, design, construction, and sales of this project. Regarding the distribution of property, it was provided that, except for compensating Huamao Company with 11,070 square meters of property, all remaining property would belong to Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company. This proves that the property area to be distributed to Huamao Company had been determined to be 11,070 square meters. To implement the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement," the project company Jiechang Company entered into the "Demolition and Relocation Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" with Huamao Company regarding the area and specific locations of the property to be distributed. Both parties should strictly perform these agreements.

Jiechang Company was not a party to the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement" but was a project company established by the cooperative parties, responsible for the planning, design, construction, and sales of the project. Based on optimizing and adjusting the project planning and design, Jiechang Company increased the original building area from 43,787 square meters to 71,549.8 square meters and obtained approval from the relevant authorities for implementation. The increased area resulted from Jiechang Company's increased investment on the same land and optimized design. Huamao Company still contributed the 26.62 mu of land and did not increase any other investment. Although Huamao Company was a joint development entity, the area to be distributed to it had been determined as 11,070 square meters in the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement." Moreover, during the development process, Huamao Company also signed the "Supplemental Agreement" with Jiechang Company regarding the building area to be distributed, further confirming the property area and specific locations to be compensated to it. Therefore, Huamao Company's request to distribute the increased area lacked sufficient grounds. Huamao Company's claim that Jiechang Company unilaterally increased the property area, resulting in unreasonable height and insufficient lighting in the shopping mall to be distributed, constituted a breach of contract during the performance of the contract and was not a reason for Huamao Company to seek an increased distribution of property area. However, given that Huamao Company had performed some preliminary development work before Jiechang Company's development, and during the project development, Huamao Company, as a cooperative party, fulfilled its cooperative obligations under the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement," and based on the principles of fairness and good faith, Jiechang Company may provide appropriate compensation to Huamao Company for the increased area resulting from its development.

Regarding Huamao Company's request that major decisions concerning the cooperative project and all pre-sale and sales activities be jointly signed, sealed, and handled by both parties, since Huamao Company signed the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement" with Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen, and Jiechang Company was not a party to that agreement but rather a project company with independent legal personality entrusted by the cooperative parties to develop the project, it enjoys the qualification to conduct independent business activities. Moreover, the development agreement also granted Jiechang Company corresponding rights. Huamao Company's claim lacked legal basis and was not supported. During the development process, Jiechang Company changed the project name to "Triumph Capital Plaza," which was approved by the Changzhi Municipal Development and Reform Commission of Shanxi Province. Huamao Company's request to restore the original name "Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street" was unreasonable, and its claim for compensation of RMB 1 million for economic losses suffered as a result was not supported due to the lack of corresponding evidence at the trial of first instance.

In summary, although Huamao Company was a joint development entity, the area to be distributed to it had been determined in the three agreements and is confirmed hereby. Jiechang Company, as the project development company, should own the increased area resulting from the development process. However, considering that Huamao Company, as a cooperative party to the project, fulfilled its obligations under the cooperation agreement, and based on the principles of fairness and good faith, Jiechang Company should appropriately compensate Huamao Company with 20% of the increased area of 27,762 square meters, with specific locations to be determined based on the principle of mixing good and bad properties. Huamao Company's other claims should be dismissed. Pursuant to Article 4 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 5, 8, and 60 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the court entered judgment: (1) Jiechang Company shall compensate Huamao Company with 5,552 square meters from the increased area, comprising 2,166 square meters of residential area, 1,000 square meters of independent shops, and 2,386 square meters of large and small shopping malls; (2) Huamao Company's other claims are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 74,087.15 shall be borne by Huamao Company in the amount of RMB 44,452.15 and by Jiechang Company in the amount of RMB 29,635.

Both Huamao Company and Jiechang Company disagreed with the judgment of first instance and appealed to this Court.

Huamao Company appealed, arguing that the judgment of first instance was inconsistent with the facts and should be modified. It requested: (1) To revoke the Civil Judgment (2005) Jin Min Chu Zi No. 1 of the Shanxi High People's Court in accordance with the law, and to modify it to: (a) order Jiechang Company to additionally distribute to Huamao Company a total of 13,881.4 square meters from the increased development and construction area of 27,762.8 square meters unilaterally expanded by Jiechang Company, at a ratio of 50% and in proportion to the area of various types of properties, based on the principle of mixing good and bad locations and levels, including an increase of 5,480.38 square meters of residential area, 2,508.37 square meters of independent shops, and 5,894.04 square meters of large and small shopping malls; (b) order Jiechang Company to restore the project name to "Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street" and cease pre-sale and sales activities under the unilaterally changed project name "Triumph Capital Plaza"; (c) order Jiechang Company to compensate Huamao Company for economic losses of RMB 1 million; (d) order that major decisions concerning the cooperative project and all sales activities be jointly handled by both parties to avoid difficulties in enforcing the distribution and the judgment; (2) and order Jiechang Company to bear all litigation costs of the first and second instances.

The main facts and reasons were: (1) Jiechang Company is the direct bearer of contractual obligations and a cooperative entity in this real estate joint development project, and it has the obligation to redistribute the newly increased building area to Huamao Company. Huamao Company, as a joint development entity in this case, has fulfilled its cooperative obligations under the cooperation agreement. Although Jiechang Company is nominally a project company, it is directly controlled and managed by Su Fulun, Chen Peisen, and Hong Kong Yiqun Company. During the performance of the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement," Jiechang Company acted on behalf of Su Fulun, Chen Peisen, and Hong Kong Yiqun Company in performing their obligations under the agreement and also directly signed various supplemental agreements related to the cooperation with Huamao Company on their behalf. All work was carried out by Jiechang Company operating as a cooperative entity. 1. The "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement" explicitly provides that Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company are responsible for the specific operation of Jiechang Company. 2. Su Fulun and Chen Peisen are the controlling shareholders of Jiechang Company, holding 98% of its shares; Chen Peisen also exercises rights on behalf of Hong Kong Yiqun Company as a nominal shareholder in Jiechang Company. 3. The obligations undertaken by Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company under the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement," including being responsible for the demolition, relocation, and costs of the part of the land other than the construction land provided by Huamao Company, paying the land transfer fee payable for that part, and being responsible for all capital investment required for the development, construction, and operation of this project, were actually performed by Jiechang Company. 4. After the signing of the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement," the parties respectively signed the "Demolition and Relocation Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" regarding outstanding matters under the cooperation agreement. Both agreements were signed by Jiechang Company on behalf of Su Fulun, Chen Peisen, and Hong Kong Yiqun Company with Huamao Company. In particular, the "Supplemental Agreement" repeatedly mentioned the cooperative relationship between the parties. 5. In the "Minutes of Coordination Meeting on Issues Raised by Huamao Company and Jiechang Company" issued by the People's Government of Chengqu District, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province, Jiechang Company also explicitly acknowledged the cooperative relationship between the parties and expressed its intention to abide by the agreements. In the list of evidence submitted in the first instance, it also acknowledged the cooperative relationship. In summary, both in fact and in written agreements, Jiechang Company has already replaced Su Fulun, Chen Peisen, and Hong Kong Yiqun Company as a party to the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement." Therefore, it has the obligation to directly assume the contractual responsibilities of this case and to redistribute the newly increased building area to Huamao Company.

(2) The 26.62 mu of development land is Huamao Company's invested land for cooperation, not land acquired by Jiechang Company through a grant. The project used a total of 35 mu of land, of which 26.62 mu (76.06%) of development land was transferred to Jiechang Company's name by Huamao Company, which bore the demolition and relocation costs itself and achieved "three connections and one leveling" based on its own granted land and as cooperative investment, pursuant to the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement" signed by both parties. This is a true reflection of the cooperation between the parties, not land acquired by Jiechang Company through a grant.

(3) The 27,762.8 square meters of building area added due to the change in project scale constitutes property formed by the investment of both parties. The 27,762.8 square meters of building area added after the change in project scale was formed on the already determined development land. With the increase in project area, the value of the land invested by Huamao Company also increased. Without Huamao Company's initial land investment, the current increased building area could not exist. Moreover, increasing the building area on the same area of land necessarily increases the project's floor area ratio, reduces green space and public facilities, and objectively diminishes the economic value of the building area originally distributable to Huamao Company.

(4) The 27,762.8 square meters of building area added in this property project was not agreed upon for distribution in the agreements between the parties and should reasonably be jointly owned by both cooperative parties.

(5) For the 27,762.8 square meters of building area added after the change in project scale, Huamao Company should be additionally distributed 50% of the property based on the principle of fairness and the principle of contribution. 1. During the performance of the contract, Huamao Company contributed its own land as capital, fulfilled its obligations of providing construction land, paying land transfer fees, carrying out demolition and relocation, being responsible for "three connections and one leveling," and handling procedures. The actual market value of its investment exceeded RMB 64 million. The actual investment by Jiechang Company and its shareholders was very small, with only a small amount of capital input in the early development stage. After the construction project began, the sources of funds were mainly pre-sale proceeds from property sales, bank loans, and advances from construction units. These operations could not have been realized without Huamao Company's initial land investment. 2. Even if the total investment of RMB 75 million stated in Jiechang Company's plan is taken as its actual input, compared with Huamao Company's actual input of RMB 64 million, the total investment ratio of the two parties would be 54% and 46%, respectively. Huamao Company's request for distribution of 50% of the newly increased area only is in accordance with the law. 3. In typical real estate project cooperation, the proportion of distribution to the party providing construction land is at least about 40% to 50% of the total area. In this case, Huamao Company not only provided the construction land but was also responsible for the demolition of most of the land. According to customary practice and the principle of good faith, Huamao Company's request for an additional 50% of the property from the area added after the scale change is reasonable and fair. 4. Huamao Company's request for an additional 50% of the newly increased building area is consistent with the principle of fairness.

(6) Jiechang Company committed multiple breaches of contract during the performance of the contract. 1. Jiechang Company unilaterally changed the project name agreed upon by both parties from "Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street" to "Triumph Capital Plaza," which seriously harmed Huamao Company's interests and constituted a breach of contract. "Huamao" is a commercial brand carefully built by Huamao Company over more than ten years of effort and is an intangible asset of Huamao Company. Using this name in the cooperative project had significant commercial advertising value and was therefore one of the prerequisites for Huamao Company's cooperation with its partners. Jiechang Company changed the project name without Huamao Company's consent, rendering the substantial advertising benefits that Huamao Company should have obtained null and void, causing significant economic losses to Huamao Company. Therefore, Huamao Company requests that Jiechang Company restore the project name to "Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street" and compensate Huamao Company for economic losses of no less than RMB 1 million. 2. Jiechang Company had no right to unilaterally change the scale of the cooperative project by increasing the total building area, which also constituted a breach of contract. According to the cooperative principles established in the "Real Estate Joint Development Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement," the "Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street" is to be developed as a whole by Jiechang Company. However, regarding issues such as overall investment, planning, design, construction, and sales, Jiechang Company should communicate with Huamao Company in a timely manner and should not act on its own to the detriment of Huamao Company's interests. Therefore, Jiechang Company's unilateral application to the Changzhi Municipal Development and Reform Commission of Shanxi Province to change the total building area constitutes both a breach of contract and a violation of the principle of good faith.

(7) Major matters of the cooperative project should be handled by both parties jointly. Due to Jiechang Company's various fraudulent and dishonest acts throughout the cooperation process, which have caused significant mental and economic losses to Huamao Company, it is evident that Jiechang Company is entirely untrustworthy. To prevent it from continuing to operate improperly, Huamao Company has the right to require joint decision-making power and joint signing and sealing with Jiechang Company on major matters involving the cooperative project and all pre-sale and sales activities, to ensure the realization of Huamao Company's distributive interests and the enforcement of the judgment.

Jiechang Company appealed, arguing that item (1) of the judgment of first instance was erroneous and should be modified based on the facts of this case and the provisions of the law. It requested: (1) To set aside item (1) of the Civil Judgment (2005) Jin Min Chu Zi No. 1 of the Shanxi High People's Court and modify it to dismiss all of Huamao Company's claims; (2) to affirm item (2) of the Civil Judgment (2005) Jin Min Chu Zi No. 1 of the Shanxi High People's Court; (3) to order Huamao Company to bear all litigation costs of the first and second instances.

Main Facts and Reasons: (1) The first instance judgment correctly found that Huamao Company's request for distribution of the increased area was insufficiently grounded, but in applying the principles of fairness and good faith, it ruled that Jiechang Company should appropriately compensate Huamao Company with an area of 5,552 square meters, which is clearly erroneous and contradictory. 1. The obligations performed by Huamao Company were all those stipulated in the three agreements, without exceeding the scope agreed upon. Only upon the premise of performing these obligations could it obtain the resettlement compensation area of 11,070 square meters as agreed in the agreements. Therefore, the first instance judgment, using the performance of the agreed obligations as a reason to apply the principles of fairness and good faith, and compensating Huamao Company from the area increased by Jiechang Company, was erroneous. 2. There was no self-initiated increase in area by Jiechang Company. The so-called increased area refers to the area beyond Huamao Company's original design plan. The agreement stipulated: "Huamao Company is responsible for handling all government approvals for Jiechang Company before construction commencement: The document Chang Zheng Ban Fa (2002) No. 1 shall be processed within 10 working days after the leaders approve the planning scheme of Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company." This shows that optimizing the design and increasing the area for the project was a consensus among the parties to the agreement; otherwise, the original design plan would suffice, and what would be the need for the planning scheme of Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company? Moreover, Huamao Company participated in the process when Jiechang Company completed the new design plan and reported the project change for approval. This is confirmed by the agreement's terms and relevant testimonies, such as that of witness Du Zimei. The resettlement compensation area of 11,070 square meters for Huamao Company was determined with its knowledge, and Huamao Company made no new contributions beyond the rights and obligations established in the three agreements. Therefore, obtaining the agreed rights by performing the agreed obligations does not constitute obvious unfairness. 3. Optimizing the design and increasing the building area were prerequisites for all parties to sign the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement." The original project approval document showed a total building area of 43,787 square meters, including 15,300 square meters of unsaleable area (underground parking, supporting facilities like kindergarten, senior citizen recreation center, property management, etc.), and the demolition area for this project was as high as 26,889 square meters (actual demolition area exceeded 30,000 square meters). On a 1:1 resettlement compensation basis, the saleable area was only 43,787 - 15,300 - 26,889 = 1,598 square meters. Without increasing the project area, Jiechang Company would incur losses. Without profit, Jiechang Company would not have signed the agreement with Huamao Company. After the new design plan was completed and the new project approval document was issued, on January 23, 2003, in an official letter from Huamao Company to Su Fulun, General Manager of Jiechang Company, it stated: "Now the 'Holiday Sunshine Plaza Floor Plan' has been approved by the urban construction planning department, and the floor plans for each level of the project have been finalized." This fully demonstrates that Huamao Company did not raise any objection to the new planning design and the new project name. The new project name "Holiday Sunshine Plaza" was issued together with matters such as the increase in project area, change of project development entity, and determination of funding sources in the new project approval document. It is impossible for Huamao Company to only know about the change of project name but not the increase in project area. Moreover, in the "Supplementary Agreement," it was clearly stated: "Regarding matters related to design changes, both parties agree that the entire project shall be constructed in accordance with the full set of construction drawings prepared by Shenzhen Design and Decoration Engineering Co., Ltd. and approved by the Changzhi City Construction Management Department." Therefore, Huamao Company was fully informed and did not raise any objections. 4. Where civil rights and interests are obviously unfair, a party may request the court to modify or revoke them within the statutory time limit, but Huamao Company did not make such a request within the statutory time limit. Furthermore, the acts of signing the "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement" and the subsequent "Supplementary Agreement" also constituted a reconfirmation of Huamao Company's own rights.

(2) The first instance judgment correctly found that Huamao Company was not a party to the cooperative development agreement, but its finding that Huamao Company was a main entity of the project cooperative development was erroneous. 1. Although the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" was nominally a cooperative development agreement, Huamao Company did not invest funds into the project company for joint operation, nor did the land after demolition become an investment into the project company, nor was it willing to bear any risks. Therefore, Huamao Company essentially did not have the subject qualification for cooperative development; it merely transferred the land to Jiechang Company, and its acquisition of rights was established in the agreement as a legal relationship of demolition and resettlement compensation without bearing any risks. The first instance judgment, which held that because the agreement stipulated obligations Huamao Company should perform (i.e., demolishing above-ground structures, achieving "three connections and one leveling," and bearing the costs incurred thereby), and thus found Huamao Company to be a main entity of the cooperative development of the project, was erroneous. These stipulations are not essential requirements of a cooperative development contract, but rather agreed obligations that the party being demolished should perform in order to transfer the land from raw land to developed land, and are one of the prerequisites for Huamao Company to obtain the agreed 11,070 square meters of area. 2. The rights and obligations among the parties to the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" were decomposed through two different legal relationships. First, parties other than Huamao Company agreed to contribute funds into Jiechang Company, and their rights and obligations were reflected in Jiechang Company according to their shareholding ratios. Second, Huamao Company and the changed project development entity, Jiechang Company, signed the "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement," and Huamao Company's rights and obligations were implemented in the legal relationship of demolition and resettlement compensation with Jiechang Company. 3. Jiechang Company, as the project company for this construction project, not only acquired the land from Huamao Company but also acquired land from other demolished entities. The rights of the demolished parties were implemented in the "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement." Jiechang Company independently bears operational risks, and in accordance with the Company Law, the rights and obligations can only be borne by the company's shareholders after the change. Huamao Company no longer holds shares in Jiechang Company and therefore cannot be recognized as a main entity of the project's cooperative development.

(3) There is only one single legal relationship of demolition and resettlement between Jiechang Company and Huamao Company. The demolition and resettlement legal relationship between the two parties was pre-agreed in the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" and was fully confirmed in the "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement." Whether it is the title of the parties signing the agreements or the detailed stipulations of substantive rights and obligations, it fully proves that the rights and obligations between the two parties constitute a legal relationship of demolition and resettlement.

The facts found by this Court in the second instance trial are the same as those found by the first instance court.

This Court holds that the three issues in dispute between the parties in the second instance are: whether the relationship between Huamao Company and Jiechang Company involved in this case is a cooperative development relationship or a demolition and resettlement compensation relationship; whether Jiechang Company breached the contract and whether it should bear liability for breach; and how the newly added area should be handled.

(I) Concerning the issue of whether the relationship between Huamao Company and Jiechang Company is a cooperative development relationship or a demolition and resettlement compensation relationship.

Viewed from the development and construction process of the project in question, before Huamao Company signed the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" with Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen, Huamao Company had already submitted the "Report on the Development and Renovation Plan of Huamao Commercial Park," obtained government approval to develop the Huamao Commercial Park, and obtained the site selection opinion letter and the construction land planning permit for the project. To facilitate development and construction, shareholders including Liu Huachuan had registered and established Jiechang Company before the signing of the agreement. The preliminary approval procedures for the project, such as project establishment and planning, were the result of Huamao Company's operations and formed the basis for the signing of the agreement. The agreement clearly stipulated the content of division and cooperation among the parties. Evidence submitted by Huamao Company and Jiechang Company shows that out of the total 19,983.19 square meters of land area for the project, 17,762.59 square meters were transferred from Huamao Company's own land, for which it had obtained land use rights, into the name of Jiechang Company, and 2,220.6 square meters were directly acquired by Jiechang Company through a listing and transfer method. Huamao Company, in accordance with the agreement, contributed its own land, for which it had land use right certificates, to the cooperative project. The stipulated content and actual performance of the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" indicate that Jiechang Company was the vehicle for the project cooperation, established to operate the cooperative project of the parties. Huamao Company and Jiechang Company were not counterparties in the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement." However, Huamao Company, as a counterparty with Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen, agreed that the project development method would use Jiechang Company as the project company for the renovation and construction of the "Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street," with the original renovation and construction unit changed from Huamao Company to Jiechang Company for renovation, construction, and operation. It was agreed that, except for the costs borne by Huamao Company for "three connections and one leveling," Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company would be responsible for providing all the funds required for the development, construction, and operation of the project, and for the specific operation of Jiechang Company and the overall planning, design, construction, and sales of the project. It was also agreed that "after the entire project is completed and sales are finalized and handed over to the property management company, the agreement terminates and the project company is dissolved." The subsequent "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement" and "Supplementary Agreement" were also premised on the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" and were directly signed between Huamao Company and Jiechang Company. Therefore, Jiechang Company had a dual status in the project cooperation: on the one hand, as the project company for the cooperative development of the project by Huamao Company, Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen; on the other hand, as the agreement was performed, it replaced Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen as the cooperative entity, continuing the project cooperation with Huamao Company, and successively signed the "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement."

A cooperative development contract for real estate is an agreement entered into by parties with the basic content of jointly contributing land use rights, funds, etc., sharing profits, and bearing risks jointly to cooperatively develop real estate. In a cooperative development contract for real estate where one party contributes funds and the other contributes acquired land use rights, the party contributing the land use rights transferring the land use rights to be jointly owned by all cooperative parties or into the name of the project company is usually an important content stipulated in the cooperative development contract; sometimes a separate land use right transfer contract may also be signed. The true intention of the parties is whether it is a cooperation with the land use rights valued as capital contribution or a simple transfer of land use rights, and whether the cooperative parties share profits and bear risks is the main basis for determination. Where the parties agree to jointly establish a special project company to develop the real estate, regardless of whether the project company is established and whether the land use rights have been registered and transferred to the project company, it does not affect the validity of the real estate cooperative development contract. In the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement," there was no stipulation that any party would obtain fixed benefits without bearing any cooperative risk regardless of whether the project was profitable or loss-making. All cooperative parties actually bore the cooperative risks. The essence of the agreement was that Huamao Company contributed the land use rights as capital to cooperate with the counterparties. Therefore, a cooperative relationship was formed between Huamao Company, Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen through the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" and the actual performance of that agreement. After the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" was signed, the "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement" and the "Supplementary Agreement" were signed for matters not fully covered by the cooperative agreement. Here, Jiechang Company was the entity of the cooperative agreement and assumed the rights and obligations of Su Fulun, Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and Chen Peisen under the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement," and was responsible for performing the relevant content stipulated therein. Therefore, an actual cooperative development relationship existed between Huamao Company and Jiechang Company. The content determined in the "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement" constituted another legal relationship formed between Huamao Company and Jiechang Company regarding specific demolition and resettlement matters.

(II) Concerning the issue of whether Jiechang Company breached the contract and whether it should bear liability for breach.

1. Whether Jiechang Company's unilateral increase in area constituted a breach. Although the newly increased 27,762.8 square meters of building area in the project was not stipulated in the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement," Jiechang Company's re-optimization of the project design and change of project approval for development and construction were in compliance with the requirements of the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" regarding the specific implementation of the project by Su Fulun and Hong Kong Yiqun Company, and their responsibility for the specific operation of Jiechang Company and the overall planning, design, construction, and sales of the project. It was an act of specifically performing the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" and did not constitute a breach of contract by unilaterally increasing the area.

2. Whether changing the name of the disputed real estate project constituted a breach. As mentioned above, Jiechang Company, being both the actual cooperative entity for the project and the project company for the cooperative parties to operate the project, was an independent legal entity project company entrusted by the cooperative parties to develop the project and enjoyed the qualifications for independent business activities. Moreover, the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" also granted Jiechang Company corresponding rights. During the development process, the project was registered under the name of Jiechang Company, and the project name was changed to "Holiday Sunshine Plaza," which Huamao Company effectively recognized in its correspondence. Later, upon Jiechang Company's application and approval by the Changzhi City Development and Planning Commission of Shanxi Province, the project name was further changed to "Triumph Plaza." Jiechang Company's change of the name of the disputed real estate project did not constitute a breach. Huamao Company's request to restore the original name "Huamao Commercial Pedestrian Street" lacked sufficient reasons, and its claim for compensation of RMB 1,000,000 for losses caused thereby, for which it did not provide corresponding evidence at trial, was correctly dismissed by the first instance court.

(III) Concerning the issue of how the newly added area should be handled.

The "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" and the "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement" were based on the Huamao Commercial Park project, with a total development and construction scale of 43,787 square meters approved by the Changzhi City Reform and Development Planning Commission under Document Chang Ji Tou Zi (2001) No. 216. The agreement stipulated that Huamao Company should be allocated 11,070 square meters of property, which was determined based on the premise of 43,787 square meters. The "Supplementary Agreement" stated: "Pursuant to the 'Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement' signed by the four parties on July 6, 2002, and the 'Demolition and Resettlement Agreement' signed by the parties, and in accordance with the spirit of the coordination meeting of the municipal and district governments, the following supplementary agreement is reached through equal negotiation on specific issues such as project allocation and compensation." It can be seen that the cooperative parties still carried out the allocation and compensation of areas based on the original "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement" and "Demolition and Resettlement Agreement" without making new arrangements for the distribution of the increased portion of the 71,549.8 square meters building area after the project optimization design. Huamao Company's claim for the allocation of the additionally increased building area was not a claim for project profit distribution as a shareholder, but a request based on the cooperative contract relationship arising from a change in the allocated property area agreed upon in the "Real Estate Cooperative Development Agreement." The newly added area was a product of the cooperative project and should logically be jointly owned by all cooperative parties. However, none of the three agreements made any further arrangement for the distribution of the newly increased 27,762.8 square meters of building area. The first instance court was correct in finding that Huamao Company's request lacked sufficient contractual basis. The 71,549.8 square meters building area of the project was approved in the name of Jiechang Company and constructed based on the approval of Document Chang Ji (2002) No. 130 by the relevant government departments. Of the total 19,983.19 square meters of land area for the project, 17,762.59 square meters were originally Huamao Company's own land for which it had obtained land use rights, and 2,220.6 square meters were directly acquired by Jiechang Company through a listing and transfer method. The first instance court, applying the principle of fairness to the newly added area not stipulated by the parties, taking into account the cooperation circumstances, determined a ratio of 20% for Huamao Company. This determination is roughly equivalent to the result of a comprehensive consideration based on the actual performance of the cooperation project, including the distribution ratio of initially agreed allocated areas and the changes in the distribution ratio during contract performance. It also accords with the actual circumstances of this case and may be affirmed.

In conclusion, the appellate requests of Huamao Company and Jiechang Company lack factual and legal basis and are not supported. Although the first instance judgment was not entirely accurate in its findings on some facts, this did not affect the actual outcome of the case and did not result in unfairness; thus, the judgment may be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 74,087.15 shall be borne by Changzhi Huamao Non-Staple Food & Fruit Products Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 44,452.15, and by Changzhi Jiechang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 29,635.00.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Cheng Xinwen

Acting Judge: Liu Yinchun

Acting Judge: Chen Chaolun

September 26, 2006

Clerk: Wang Dongying

[Introduction of Presiding Judge]

Cheng Xinwen, senior judge: born in 1963, Master of Laws, served as Deputy Chief Judge of the First Civil Division of the Supreme People's Court from 2005.
